findings.where: The MMM Infra logo in two places: the header lockup on the slate hero, where the arches and the 'MMM INFRA' wordmark are both reversed to warm white (desktop-01, phone-01), and the footer mark on warm white, where both are house grey (desktop-07, phone-05)
findings.fault: The client's logo has grey arches and a blue wordmark, but neither placement shows it. The header uses an all-white version the client does not hold. The footer recolours the blue wordmark to grey, even though the full-colour logo would sit on the warm white ground at 4.79:1. So the page shows two home-made versions of the logo and never the real one.
findings.who_objects: Mark, and anyone who keeps his brand. The blue wordmark is one of the two house colours the founder asked every tile to keep. Recolouring a mark, or making a reversed version without the client's agreement, breaks the logo rules any brand guideline sets. In the footer, where nothing stops the real logo being used, the change only makes the brand weaker.

findings.where: Article specimen, the 'Lectures' list item under the article's last line ('Streamlining the PPP Process…', 'Lecture · 23 April 2026') (desktop-05, phone-04)
findings.fault: The lecture's title and its date line start about 4 px to the right of the 'Lectures' label, the hairlines and the article's left edge. That small step looks like leftover padding from the card styling that was removed. On a page with one text edge, it reads as a slip, not as an indent someone meant.
findings.who_objects: A careful reader, or the founder judging craft. The article claims everything sits on one rhythm and one edge, and Angélique will repeat this item for every PDF in the list, so the slip would show on every row.

findings.where: Article specimen, the subhead 'So, what are the key ‘chapter topics’?' compared with the article title above it and the other serif headings on the page (desktop-05, phone-03)
findings.fault: The subhead is set in a semibold serif. The article title, the hero line and 'Unhurried, settled, clear.' are all light or regular, so the lower heading is heavier than the title it sits under. The type pair panel lists 330 for the line, 400 for text and 700 for the wordmark, and this weight is not among them.
findings.who_objects: A reader taking in the article. The heavier subhead pulls the eye away from the title, which turns the order upside down. Angélique would also be copying a heading style the page's own type system never defined into every article.
